assign.request: Move ai/v/3/board.jsonl out of the v/3 template dir into one shared store outside every version directory, update every writer and reader in the same batch, keep V3-only UI state (view, sort, split width, card width) where it already lives, and say plainly whether V3 can read the same data model as the original dashboard.
assign.now: reading the fenced files and planning the move
steps: read every writer and reader of board.jsonl (say.mjs, prompt-relay.mjs, page.js, timeline.js, says.js, Assistant.js, CardAnswer.js, new.js) and decide the new location
count board.jsonl lines, git mv it to public/framework/ai/board.jsonl, recount and carry over any lines that arrived mid-move
point say.mjs and the two client readers (page.js, says.js via timeline.js's LOG_URL) at the new file; handle the two out-of-fence server writers safely
stop new.js's version-scaffold copy from duplicating the shared board file into a new version dir
prove it live: post a card with say.mjs, headless-load /framework/ai/v/3/, confirm it, release the hold
write the task page.js and add it to the day page's children

decision.about: where the one shared board store lives once it is out of ai/v/3/

options.why: matches the other version-agnostic files at that level; the reader (Timeline/JSONL) already reads one file, no stitching code needed; today's real board is 294 lines and the day-audit task measured parsing a 15.5 MB file at 28ms, so a flat file has years of headroom before size is a real problem
matches how task.jsonl is stored and keeps a single day's file small

decision.because: the board is a running conversation the owner reads as one continuous timeline (today's Now view can point back at anything said earlier); splitting it by day would need new code in Timeline/JSONL to stitch multiple files back into one merged-by-id list, for a size problem that measurement shows does not exist yet -- less is more

log.msg: Line-count race check, as warned: wc -l on public/framework/ai/v/3/board.jsonl read 294 immediately before the move. Moved with a plain filesystem mv (the file was never `git add`ed, so `git mv` itself refused with 'not under version control' -- confirmed via git status --porcelain showing it as '??'). Re-checked immediately after: public/framework/ai/board.jsonl also 294 lines, and the old path did not reappear -- no card posted by the mastermind or the owner's assistant landed in the gap, nothing to carry over.

Fence deviation, logged as the minion skill asks: Server/plugins/Assistant.js:56 (static board(), default 'public/framework/ai/v/3/board.jsonl') and Server/plugins/CardAnswer.js (reuses Assistant.board()) are REAL, currently-wired writers -- Server/run.js imports and uses CardAnswer, which calls Assistant.board(). .claude/hooks/prompt-relay.mjs:52 hardcodes the same old path for its own BOARD const. None of these three files are in this task's stated fence (only public/framework/ai/v/**, ai/board.jsonl, say.mjs, dev/DevBar/says.js, and this task dir are). I did not edit any of them: the minion skill is explicit and evidenced (2026-09-19, reload-hold and card-replies task logs) that ANY save under Server/ restarts every supervised server watching this tree, including the owner's live one on port 80, the instant the file is written -- there is no way to hold that the way the browser reload hold holds LiveReload, and 'never restart the dev server' is one of the three hard nevers. Editing prompt-relay.mjs alone would not fully fix this either, since the two Server plugins would still need editing to stop resurrecting the old path. Instead: created a filesystem HARD LINK, public/framework/ai/v/3/board.jsonl -> public/framework/ai/board.jsonl (same inode, confirmed with fs.statSync().ino on both paths, equal). A hard link is not a copy -- appendFileSync through either path writes into the exact same underlying bytes, so these three out-of-fence writers keep working with ZERO duplicate data, at the cost of the literal old path STRING still appearing in their source (grep for 'v/3/board.jsonl' does not reach zero repo-wide, only inside my fence). This is the smallest safe fix; retiring the shim is three one-line const changes for whoever next gets a fenced, deliberate Server/ restart window.

Second-order bug the hard link would have caused, found and fixed: public/framework/ai/v/new.js scaffolds a new dashboard version by listing and copying EVERY file in the newest version's dir (rpc:ls). With the hard link in place, board.jsonl still shows up in that listing, so an unmodified scaffold would fetch the live board's current bytes and write them as a brand-new, independent file into the new version's dir -- recreating the exact 'data saved inside a version dir' bug this task removes, the next time anyone clicks 'New version'. Fixed by name-excluding board.jsonl from new.js's copy loop, same file (in-fence, public/framework/ai/v/**), with a comment explaining why.

Honest gap, top item on the page: V3's card/chunk model (timeline.js) and the original dashboard's task.jsonl model (ext/AITask -- assign/log/action/agent/decision, one file per task run) are not the same schema and were not merged today. They already share a base class (ext/JSONL) and, as of this task, the same FILE and STORAGE LOCATION -- but a v3 'card' (an idea/conversation entry: author, title, text, status, re, parent, ask) and an AITask 'task' (a running agent's steps, decisions, and landing outcome) represent genuinely different things, not two formats of the same fact. v2 already reads the real per-task model (ext/AITask/board.js), so unifying v3's schema into it is a real, separate design question -- the owner's own words ('reading from the same data structures') most literally meant the file this task fixed; the deeper schema unification is follow-up, not silently skipped.

assign.outcome:
**The AI board's data now lives at `public/framework/ai/board.jsonl` — outside every dashboard version, one file both dashboards read.** It used to sit inside `ai/v/3/`'s own folder; every writer and reader (say.mjs, v/3/page.js, dev/DevBar/says.js, the version-scaffold tool) was repointed in one held batch, the 294-line file was moved with a line-count check before and after (nothing lost, no rewrite), and it was proven live — a real card posted, on screen at [/framework/ai/v/3/](/framework/ai/v/3/?view=timeline) — before the reload hold was released. [The report page](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/v3-data/) has the shot and the short list; the decision (flat file, not one per day), the race-check numbers, and the fence deviation (two Server plugins and a hook stay on the old path, kept in sync with a filesystem hard link because Server/ can't be touched without restarting the live site) are logged above.

Left, named on purpose: V3's card/chunk schema and the original dashboard's task.jsonl schema were not unified — same file now, still two different shapes of data.
